raw_response:
Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates complete opacification (white-out) of the left hemithorax with a distinct mediastinal shift to the right, which is the classic radiographic appearance of a massive pleural effusion pushing structures away from the affected side. In contrast, consolidation typically shows no shift or slight shift toward the lesion, and atelectasis would cause a shift toward the opacity.
